interest: U.S. resisted British and Chinese efforts in the FEC to revise Japan's 1947 Constitution.
keywords: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
overview: This file contains State Department records from February to December 1949 concerning the formal review of the Japanese Constitution ('Peace Constitution') by the Far Eastern Commission (FEC), the Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (SCAP), and the U.S. Government. In accordance with the FEC policy decision FEC-031/41, the Commission undertook a two-year review of the new constitution, prompting comments and inquiries from member states including the United Kingdom, China, and Australia. U.S. officials in Washington and Tokyo consistently maintained that the constitution had functioned successfully, opposing FEC efforts to recommend formal amendments or forward Commission debates to General Douglas MacArthur or the Japanese Diet. Key legal and constitutional issues addressed include the civil rights of aliens under Article 17 and the State Redress Law, judicial review powers of the Supreme Court over local public safety ordinances, the Cabinet's authority to dissolve the House of Representatives under Articles 7 and 69, imperial succession, and the preservation of a bicameral Diet. The documentation consists of internal State Department policy and legal analyses, formal communications between the FEC, the Department of State, SANACC, and SCAP, General MacArthur's second-anniversary public address on the constitution, and congressional correspondence involving Senator Lyndon B. Johnson regarding academic distribution of the constitution.

subfiles.about: Recommendations for the U.S. member of the Far Eastern Commission regarding the constitutional review and British comments on alien rights in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Alice L. Dunning urges the U.S. to oppose FEC moves, including British objections on aliens' rights, to reopen Japan's Constitution.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Alice L. Dunning to Max W. Bishop on the Review of the Japanese Constitution

subfiles.about: Transmittal of proposed U.S. comments responding to Chinese inquiries regarding the Japanese Constitution in Committee 3 of the FEC.
subfiles.summary: Conrad E. Snow sends FE a draft of U.S. responses to eight Chinese questions on the Japanese Constitution in FEC Committee 3.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Conrad E. Snow to FE on Chinese Comments on the Constitution

subfiles.about: Detailed legal analysis addressing eight constitutional questions and proposals submitted by the Chinese member of Committee 3.
subfiles.from: United States Member of Committee 3, Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.summary: U.S. member's replies to eight Chinese questions on the Japanese Constitution, covering Diet dissolution, succession, bicameralism and amendment.
subfiles.title: Statement of U.S. Member of Committee 3 Relative to Chinese Comments on the Constitution

subfiles.about: Assessment of Japanese political sentiment and public opinion regarding potential revisions to the postwar constitution.
subfiles.summary: USPOLAD Tokyo reports no real Japanese sentiment for amending the new constitution; parties and occupation officials consider it working well.
subfiles.title: Airgram A-106 from USPOLAD Tokyo to the Secretary of State on Japanese Sentiment Regarding the Constitution

subfiles.about: Transmittal of an approved Far Eastern Commission message to General MacArthur regarding the review of the Japanese Constitution.
subfiles.summary: Frank McCoy sends Acheson the FEC message to SCAP on reviewing the Japanese Constitution, approved May 5, 1949, with four abstentions.
subfiles.title: Letter from Frank McCoy to Secretary of State Dean Acheson Transmitting FEC Message to SCAP

subfiles.about: Certified policy communication highlighting three specific constitutional problems for General MacArthur's attention.
subfiles.summary: FEC message to SCAP questioning the Constitution's protection of aliens' rights, Supreme Court review under Article 81, and Diet dissolution under Articles 7 and 69.
subfiles.title: Far Eastern Commission Message to SCAP Relative to the Review of the Japanese Constitution

subfiles.about: Duplicate copy of Chairman McCoy's letter forwarding the FEC message on constitutional review to the Secretary of State.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate of Frank H. McCoy's letter transmitting the FEC message on the Japanese Constitution, adopted May 5, 1949.
subfiles.title: Duplicate Letter from Frank H. McCoy to Secretary of State Dean Acheson Transmitting FEC Message to SCAP

subfiles.about: Duplicate text of the Far Eastern Commission's communication to SCAP on alien rights, judicial review, and Diet dissolution.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate FEC message to SCAP raising aliens' rights, Article 81 judicial review, and Diet dissolution under Articles 7 and 69.
subfiles.title: Duplicate Message from the Far Eastern Commission to SCAP on the Review of the Japanese Constitution

subfiles.about: Internal transmittal recommending approval of a memorandum forwarding the FEC constitutional review message to SANACC.
subfiles.summary: Niles W. Bond asks Butterworth to sign a memo sending the FEC constitutional message via SANACC and the Joint Chiefs to MacArthur.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Niles W. Bond to W. Walton Butterworth Regarding Transmittal of FEC Message to SANACC

subfiles.about: Formal request to forward the Far Eastern Commission's constitutional review message to General MacArthur via the JCS.
subfiles.summary: Butterworth asks SANACC to send the FEC message on the Japanese Constitution, passed seven to zero on May 5, 1949, to MacArthur.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from W. Walton Butterworth to the Secretary, SANACC on Message to SCAP from FEC

subfiles.about: Authorization for the U.S. member of the FEC to enter General MacArthur's second-anniversary constitutional message into the record.
subfiles.summary: Butterworth authorizes the U.S. FEC member to enter MacArthur's May 3, 1949 address on the Constitution's second anniversary into the record.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from W. Walton Butterworth to the U.S. Member, FEC Authorizing Statement Quoting General MacArthur
subfiles.to: United States Member, Far Eastern Commission

subfiles.about: Notification of transmittal by the Joint Chiefs of Staff of the FEC message to General MacArthur.
subfiles.summary: George H. Haselton of SANACC sends State four copies of the Joint Chiefs' message to SCAP, one for the FEC.
subfiles.title: Memorandum SANA-6386 from George H. Haselton to the Secretary of State on Message Transmitted to SCAP

subfiles.about: Confirmation to the Far Eastern Commission that its constitutional review message was transmitted to General MacArthur by the JCS.

subfiles.title: Memorandum from Max W. Bishop to the Secretary General, FEC on Transmittal of Message to SCAP

subfiles.about: Constituent request forwarded by Senator Johnson for copies of the postwar Japanese Constitution for university instruction.

subfiles.about: Confirmation of arrangements made with the Far Eastern Commission to supply copies of the Japanese Constitution to the University of Texas.
